title: Partnering with Etched: Building the Inference Machine
gist: Sequoia led a $300M Series C in Etched at a $10B pre-money valuation, arguing that inference — not training — is on track to become the largest market in the world and that Etched is the only post-ChatGPT-era hardware startup with production-ready custom silicon shipping in 2026. The pitch rests on two claimed research breakthroughs (low voltage inference and cluster-scale memory), a full-reticle A0 tape-out at TSMC, and a 40-day cluster bring-up hitting Pareto-dominant throughput-interactivity curves.

insights.claim: Inference is argued to be on the path to becoming the largest market in the world, ultimately powering every storefront, movie, medical encounter, video game, lawsuit and line of code.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Frames inference compute — not training clusters — as the durable revenue pool; favors names levered to serving volume and cost-per-token rather than one-off training capex cycles.
insights.quote: Inference is on the path to becoming the largest market in the world.

insights.claim: Building an inference-specific system is now explicitly described as consensus, whereas in 2022 the same bet was deeply contrarian — meaning the edge has shifted from having the idea to executing on silicon.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Expect a crowded field of inference-ASIC entrants; differentiation and pricing power will come from shipped production hardware, not architecture claims, so screen entrants on tape-outs and customer racks.
insights.quote: Today, the inference market is so obviously large that building an inference-specific system is consensus. Back in 2022, when Gavin, Chris, and Rob were still in their dorm rooms at Harvard, that bet was deeply contrarian.

insights.claim: The intelligence race is characterized as fundamentally compute constrained, with the binding optimization being maximum intelligence per watt at the limits of physics.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: If intelligence output is power-bound rather than capital-bound, value accrues to whoever improves perf-per-watt — a read-through to power infrastructure, advanced packaging and low-voltage design IP.
insights.quote: The intelligence race is fundamentally compute constrained. Pushing the limits of physics to deliver the maximum intelligence per watt

themes.theme: Architecture: the cluster is the unit of compute

insights.claim: The unit of compute is described as having moved from the chip to the rack to the cluster, so Etched designs cluster-scale inference systems rather than standalone chips.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for evaluating AI hardware: vendors selling only a chip are competing at the wrong altitude; system-level integration (networking, memory, power delivery) is where margin sits.
insights.quote: As the unit of compute has moved from the chip to the rack to the cluster, Etched has designed for that reality, building not just chips, but cluster-scale inference systems.
insights.locator: As the unit of compute has moved

insights.claim: Etched claims two specific research breakthroughs — low voltage inference and cluster-scale memory — each presented as an architectural choice producing step-change gains in throughput and latency.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Low-voltage operation and pooled cluster memory are the two levers that most directly attack inference cost per token; watch whether incumbents respond with similar voltage/memory-pooling designs.
insights.quote: Etched has pioneered several research breakthroughs – low voltage inference and cluster-scale memory
insights.locator: Over the past years, Etched has pioneered

insights.claim: Etched's system is claimed to excel in throughput and interactivity across the full span of frontier model families — large sparse mixture-of-experts, dense transformers, and alternative architectures such as Mamba.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Directly rebuts the standard bear case on inference ASICs — that fixed-function silicon gets stranded when model architectures shift; verify with third-party benchmarks before underwriting it.
insights.quote: from large sparse MoEs, to dense transformers, to alternative architectures entirely, like Mamba

insights.claim: The core risk in custom AI silicon is that models change every few weeks, context lengths stretch, attention gets reinvented, and the dense/sparse mix keeps shifting, so a hardware team must simultaneously iterate at model speed and push the hardware frontier.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Design-cycle velocity, not peak FLOPS, is the diligence question for any inference-chip investment; a single strong tape-out is not evidence of a franchise.
insights.quote: Models change every few weeks, context lengths stretch, attention gets reinvented, the mix of dense and sparse keeps shifting.
insights.locator: Novel computing hardware is among the hardest

insights.claim: Etched is claimed to be the first post-ChatGPT-era company with a successful full-reticle A0 chip tape-out on TSMC's leading-edge nodes, taped out earlier in 2026.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: A first-silicon-works A0 on a leading node is the rarest de-risking event in chip startups; it compresses time-to-revenue and is the main justification for the $10B mark.
insights.quote: the first post-ChatGPT-era company with a successful full-reticle A0 chip tape-out on TSMC's leading-edge nodes
insights.locator: Earlier this year, Etched taped out

insights.claim: Etched brought up its first cluster of chips and ran inference on a wide range of frontier AI models in a span of just 40 days, claiming Pareto-dominant performance on industry-standard throughput-interactivity curves.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: A 40-day bring-up is the concrete, checkable metric in the piece; if the Pareto-dominance claim survives independent benchmarking it is a genuine threat to incumbent inference margins.
insights.quote: in a span of just 40 days, the Etched team brought up their first cluster of chips to run inference on a wide range of frontier AI models, achieving Pareto dominant performance
insights.locator: Then, in a span of just 40 days

insights.claim: Etched stood up a live lab in San Jose to host its first racks and opened an office in Taiwan to colocate with suppliers and expedite testing, treating physical proximity to the supply chain as a speed advantage.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Colocation with Taiwanese suppliers is an underrated operational moat in hardware startups and a reminder that Taiwan concentration risk sits under every AI-silicon thesis.
insights.quote: opening an office in Taiwan to colocate with suppliers and expedite testing
insights.locator: standing up a live lab in San Jose

insights.claim: Etched is described as the only post-ChatGPT-era hardware startup with production-ready custom silicon ready to ship in 2026, with earliest customers already receiving access to the product.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Sets a specific falsifiable checkpoint: if 2026 shipments and customer deployments do not materialize, the exclusivity claim and the valuation both break.
insights.quote: Etched is the only post-ChatGPT-era hardware startup with production-ready custom silicon, ready to ship in 2026.

insights.claim: Sequoia led a $300 million Series C in Etched at a $10 billion pre-money valuation, joined by Jane Street, Andreessen Horowitz, Diffusion and SK Hynix.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: SK Hynix in the cap table signals memory-supply alignment for the cluster-scale memory design, and Jane Street's presence marks trading-firm capital moving into private AI silicon — a marker of late-cycle private AI pricing.
insights.quote: leading their $300 Million Series C at a $10 Billion pre-money valuation, joined by our friends at Jane Street, Andreessen Horowitz, Diffusion, and SK Hynix
insights.locator: We are delighted to be partnering with Etched

insights.claim: The stated investment rationale is not the Gen 1 product but 'the machine that builds the machine' — the team's capacity to keep shipping successive generations of inference hardware rather than a single tape-out.
insights.speaker: Sequoia Arc
insights.so_what: Underwriting a repeat-tape-out capability rather than one product is how to value hardware franchises; it also means the $10B mark prices multiple future generations, leaving little cushion if Gen 2 slips.
insights.quote: we are partnering with Etched because we believe they have built the rarest thing in this industry: the machine that builds the machine
insights.locator: Etched has built a beautiful machine in Gen 1
